nodes.description: Heterozygous truncating IL6ST variants encode a gp130 receptor that keeps its extracellular and transmembrane domains but loses the distal cytoplasmic tail (the recycling motif and the four STAT3-recruiting tyrosines). The mutant receptor accumulates at the cell surface and poisons signalling complexes formed with wild-type gp130 - a dominant-negative, not a haploinsufficiency, mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant-negative mutations in human IL6ST underlie hyper-IgE syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant-negative mutations in human IL6ST underlie hyper-IgE syndrome.
evidence.snippet: L708*, I719fs, C733*, S742fs, S754*, Y759*, and T761fs mutants, the only mutants identified that accumulate at the cell surface, exert a strong DN effect for all GP130-dependent cytokines tested, including IL-6 trans-signaling (IL-6/IL-6Rα).
